context.description: One run is live in a directory at a time (owner ruling 3)

evidence.trustReason: Fresh-context review at HEAD 5fb09be29c (after the harness.ts change c8ffccfee1); test unchanged since 6841bc0e5d; trial bun test 2 pass 0 fail. Given a live run of the release-notes spec in a directory: test 1 starts it through the real TaskCommand.run with the real TaskHarness lease, the real event store and a seeded git instance; the registry's run mode runs the job's own effect, so run.started and two task.started are stored, harness.running is true, harness.live holds {runID, spec, path} and status.json exists (only the session side and the job registry are test boundaries). When /task runs for a valid spec in the same directory: it runs for example-scenarios, a task folder of it, and release-notes again. Then it starts nothing and answers one line naming the live run's spec and path: each reply equals exactly the EXPERIENCE 'Busy reply' text (written out literally in the test, so it is independent of the code) and has no newline; no new job start, no fact under the other spec's run id, the lease unchanged, status.json still the live run's and not refused, and the live run gains no run.* fact. And a claim whose background job does not start is released so the next /task is not busy: test 2 makes BackgroundJob.start die (/task fails, no start, lease none), then answers as a job already running elsewhere (already-going-on reply, lease none), then the next /task claims, starts its job with parentSessionId and holds the lease; test 1 also shows the directory free after the live run is cancelled. Minor observation, not a gap against the Gherkin: the live run's path equals its spec path, so the test does not separate the two fields; the Gherkin's given is a whole-spec run. Every step is asserted specifically on the real code.
